newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany sends home group of Vietnamese.
newsitem.headline: Germany sends home group of Vietnamese.

text.p: Germany sent home to Vietnam on Tuesday the first large group of former Vietnamese "guest workers" who have been living illegally in the country, the interior ministry said.
Nearly one year after Vietnam agreed to take back 40,000 Vietnamese living in Germany, the first charter plane carrying 239 passengers departed from Schoenefeld airport in Berlin bound for Hanoi.
The ministry said that a total of 657 Vietnamese had been repatriated to Vietnam during the last year, but in smaller numbers aboard scheduled flights.
Most of the Vietnamese were "guest workers" brought here in the 1980s by East Germany's communist government.

Most were left without legal jobs after German unity and many got caught up in a vicious turf war waged throughout the east between rival Vietnamese gangs dealing in the lucrative trade of cigarette smuggling.
In exchange for taking its citizens back, Bonn gave Vietnam 200 million marks ($130 million) in development aid after the repatriation accord was signed.
Bonn had threatened to delay the payments earlier this year because it said Vietnam was moving too slowly in taking its citizens back.
